hero.lead: A nation of 285.7 million across seventeen thousand islands, where nine in ten cook with clean fuel and the World Bank has committed more than $4.4 billion since 2025.

capital.heading: Indonesia finances at scale and pioneered the green sukuk. Next, safe water in every home.

record.text: General government debt, % of GDP, 2024; the IMF projects 41.0% for 2025
First Growth and Jobs Development Policy Loan, approved August 2026: expected to add about 1% to GDP by 2030, equal to around 2.4 million more and better-paid jobs
The Republic’s first panda bonds, July 2026: about $1.03 billion, with orders of 2.4 times
MIGA-guaranteed loan to Bank Mandiri, August 2026: it could benefit more than 190,000 small businesses
The world’s first sovereign green sukuk, issued February 2018

register.name: Inaugural sovereign panda bonds
register.detail: Priced 23 July 2026 · Settled 30 July 2026 · 3-year CNY 5.6B at 1.90%, 5-year CNY 1.4B at 2.19%
register.note: About $1.03 billion; orders of CNY 17 billion, 2.4 times the issue
register.text: The Republic’s first panda bonds, sold in China’s onshore market with an onshore AAA rating. They widen the investor base that finances the state budget.

register.name: US dollar and euro notes, with a euro SDG bond
register.detail: Settled 29 May 2026 · 5-year $750M at 5.030%, 10-year $1.25B at 5.690% · 7-year SDG €600M at 4.500%, 12-year €650M at 5.125%
register.note: Equivalent in all; the SDG tranche is €600M
register.text: Notes in dollars and euros for the state budget. The Republic intends to invest an amount equal to the net proceeds of the 7-year SDG tranche in projects that may qualify as eligible expenditures under its Sustainable Government Securities Framework.

register.name: Samurai bonds, with blue bonds
register.detail: 2026 · 7-year and 10-year yields set at the lowest end of guidance · The Republic’s fourth blue bond issue since 2023
register.note: About $1.08 billion
register.text: Yen bonds sold in Japan, among them blue bonds, the Republic’s fourth issue of blue bonds since 2023. They widen the investor base that finances the state budget.

register.name: Offshore renminbi and euro bonds
register.detail: Priced 25 February 2026 · Settled 4 March 2026 · CNH 4.5B, 3.5B and 1.25B at 2.450%, 2.650% and 3.050% for 3, 5 and 10 years · €1.2B, €800M and €700M at 4.100%, 4.460% and 4.970% for 8, 12 and 20 years
register.note: Offshore renminbi and euro in one offering
register.text: A dual-currency offering for the state budget: offshore renminbi bonds in three tenors and euro bonds out to 20 years.

register.name: US dollar notes
register.detail: 2026 · 5-year, 10-year and 30-year tranches
register.note: SEC-registered senior notes
register.text: International bonds sold to global investors for the 2026 state budget, in three tranches out to 30 years.

register.name: Global Sukuk, prefunding for 2026
register.detail: Priced 19 November 2025 · Issued 1 December 2025 · 5-year at 4.50%, 10-year at 5.00%
register.note: Raised in 2025 for the 2026 budget
register.text: Sharia-compliant certificates sold to global investors in advance of the 2026 budget year, in 5-year and 10-year tranches.

register.name: Global Sukuk with a 30-year green tranche
register.detail: Priced 25 June 2024 · Settled 2 July 2024 · 5-year $750M at 5.10%, 10-year $1B at 5.20%, 30-year green $600M at 5.50%
register.note: Green tranche $600M; orders of $4.5 billion
register.text: Sharia-compliant bonds sold to global investors, with a 30-year green tranche for climate and environmental projects under the Republic’s green framework. Orders reached $4.5 billion, more than 1.9 times the issue.

register.name: Global Sukuk with a 30-year green tranche
register.detail: Priced 3 June 2021 · Settled 9 June 2021 · 5-year $1.25B at 1.50%, 10-year $1B at 2.55%, 30-year green $750M at 3.55%
register.note: Green tranche $750M; orders of $10.3 billion
register.text: Sharia-compliant bonds for the state budget, with a 30-year green tranche, the Republic’s fourth global green sukuk. Orders reached $10.3 billion, more than 3.4 times the issue.

register.name: Sovereign green sukuk, first issuance
register.detail: Issued February 2018
register.note: The world’s first sovereign green sukuk
register.text: The world’s first sovereign green sukuk, for projects that mitigate or adapt to climate change and preserve biodiversity. Indonesia has since added green tranches to its global sukuk, among them in 2021 and 2024.

register.name: First Growth and Jobs Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Approved 6 August 2026 · IBRD · First of two operations
register.note: Expected to add about 1% to GDP by 2030, equal to around 2.4 million more and better-paid jobs
register.text: Budget support for reforms that ease business licensing, deepen the financial sector, including housing finance for small businesses, and lay foundations for resilient jobs, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Local Service Delivery Improvement Project
register.detail: Approved 18 December 2025 · Starts with 30 local governments
register.note: Solid waste services for more than 15 million people
register.text: Strengthens solid waste services and infrastructure, starting with 30 local governments. It aims to give more than 15 million Indonesians cleaner surroundings and better protect 10 million from climate risks, for the shelter and health standards.

register.name: Electricity Network Transformation (I-ENET)
register.detail: Approved September 2025 · Step-up loan
register.note: With $491M from PLN and $342M of private capital expected
register.text: Modernises the distribution grid of Java, Madura and Bali for about 20 million people, with 300 MW of rooftop solar to be integrated, for the energy standard.

register.name: Productive and Sustainable Investment DPL
register.detail: Approved June 2025 · Development policy loan
register.note: Financial sector and renewable procurement
register.text: Helps remove obstacles to procuring renewable energy technology, by reducing local content requirements, and introduces land value capture to draw private capital into infrastructure.

register.name: Sustainable Least-Cost Electrification-2 (ISLE-2)
register.detail: Approved June 2025 · $600M IBRD loan with $28M of grants · Step-up loan
register.note: Power for 3.5 million people; 540 MW of solar and wind
register.text: Brings electricity to 3.5 million people in Kalimantan and Sumatra, with 540 MW of solar and wind, for the energy standard.

register.name: Financial Market Deepening Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: Approved 1 October 2026
register.note: Capital markets, digital finance and transition finance
register.text: Supports deeper capital markets, safer digital financial services with stronger rules for digital assets and cybersecurity, and sustainable and transition finance. The first subprogram is backed by $650 million of ADB financing.

register.name: Climate Adaptation and Green Resilience Program, Sub-Program 1
register.detail: Approved 26 September 2026 · Sovereign · Policy-based · First of two sub-programmes of $500M
register.note: Reforms for a climate-adaptive rural economy and resilient local services
register.text: Supports policy and institutional reforms that strengthen climate resilience in rural areas, ecosystems and local service delivery, in agriculture, water, forests and mangroves, for the food and water standards.

register.name: Accelerating Decentralization for Improved Local Governance Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: Announced 16 September 2026 · Program of $650 million equivalent
register.note: Equivalent; local budgets, fiscal data and fairer property tax
register.text: Supports coordination of public funds between central and local governments, a national digital platform for fiscal data, fairer property tax valuation and budgeting that protects women and girls. Local governments manage 35% to 40% of public spending, including on education, health care and local infrastructure.

register.name: Boosting Productivity through Human Capital Development Program, Subprogram 3
register.detail: Announced 10 December 2025 · Policy-based · Third subprogram
register.note: Preventive care, skills training and better-targeted social assistance
register.text: Supports wider preventive care in health insurance, skills training through the Prakerja programme, which has trained more than 18 million people, and social assistance targeted through a single national socio-economic database, for the health, education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Accelerating Indonesia’s Clean Energy Transition Program, Phase 1
register.detail: Announced 19 November 2025 · Results-based loan to PLN · 2026 to 2031
register.note: Expected to draw over $1 billion of private investment
register.text: A results-based loan to the state power company PLN for grid strengthening in Java-Madura-Bali, Sumatra and Sulawesi, expected to mobilise over $1 billion of private investment in 1,800 MW of utility-scale solar and wind. It comes with $30 million of ADB-managed cofinancing and a $3 million grant, for the energy standard.

register.name: Geothermal Power Generation Project, second additional financing
register.detail: Announced 31 October 2025 · Loan to Geo Dipa Energy
register.note: Two geothermal plants in Java, 55 MW each
register.text: A loan to the state-owned Geo Dipa Energy for two geothermal power plants in Java of 55 MW each, for the energy standard.

register.name: RSAB Harapan Kita Construction and Integration of Three Diamond Hospitals Project
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2025 · Sovereign
register.note: Mother and child hospital beds from 271 to 550
register.text: Builds the new RSAB Harapan Kita mother and child hospital, raising its beds from 271 to 550, and links it with the Harapan Kita cardiovascular hospital and the Dharmais cancer hospital as one integrated complex, for the health standard.

register.name: Solid Waste Management for Sustainable Urban Development Project
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2025 · Sovereign
register.note: Waste treatment, landfill upgrades and circular-economy grants
register.text: AIIB financing for waste treatment facilities, landfill upgrades, institutional strengthening, community programmes and circular-economy grants.

register.name: Competitiveness, Industrial Modernization, and Trade Acceleration Program, Subprogram 3
register.detail: Announced 15 October 2025 · Policy-based · Third subprogram
register.note: Investment climate, trade and small businesses
register.text: Supports reforms that make Indonesia more attractive for investment, cut trade barriers through automatic licensing and support small businesses, including those owned by women, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition Program, Subprogram 1
register.detail: Approved 20 September 2024 · Policy-based loan · First of two subprograms
register.note: Reforms for the shift to clean power
register.text: Supports renewable energy regulation, stronger governance and finances in the energy sector, and a fair and inclusive transition toward Indonesia’s 2050 net-zero goal for power, for the energy standard.

register.name: Competitiveness, Industrial Modernization, and Trade Acceleration Program, Subprogram 2
register.detail: Approved September 2023
register.note: Investment climate, trade logistics and local businesses
register.text: Supports investment-climate reforms, digital trade logistics and stronger local businesses, including women-owned enterprises, for livelihood.

register.name: Result-Based Loan Accelerating Indonesia Clean Energy Transition
register.detail: Signed 15 July 2026 · Loan to PLN · 2026 to 2031
register.note: Part of $1,509 million of cofinancing for the programme
register.text: An AFD loan to the state power company PLN for clean electricity supply, grid upgrades that integrate renewable power and stronger institutions, for the energy standard.

register.name: Hululais Geothermal Power Plant Project
register.detail: Signed 30 March 2026 · Japanese ODA loan · Bengkulu Province
register.note: Two geothermal plants for the Sumatra grid
register.text: Finances two geothermal power plants, transmission, substation and distribution facilities in Bengkulu, to improve power supply in the Sumatra system, for the energy standard.

register.name: Competitiveness, Industrial Modernization and Trade Acceleration Program, Subprogram 3
register.detail: Signed 30 March 2026 · Japanese ODA loan
register.note: Business environment, trade and company growth
register.text: Japanese financing for the same reform programme as the ADB loan: a better business and investment environment, fewer trade barriers and support for business expansion, for the livelihood standard.

register.name: Policy-based loan for the Affordable and Sustainable Energy Transition Program
register.detail: Signed 30 June 2025 · Loan to the Government of Indonesia · Co-financed with ADB and AFD
register.note: Germany’s support under the energy transition partnership
register.text: A KfW loan that supports the clean energy policy framework and the governance and finances of the energy sector, under the Just Energy Transition Partnership, for the energy standard.

register.name: MIGA-guaranteed social loan to Bank Mandiri
register.detail: Announced 6 August 2026 · HSBC loan in two tranches · Three years
register.note: Could benefit more than 190,000 small businesses
register.text: An HSBC loan to Bank Mandiri, covered by two MIGA guarantees, for loans to small businesses under the KUR programme: retail trade and service businesses, street vendors, and food crop and aquaculture enterprises, with a focus on women-led microenterprises. It is MIGA’s first financial sector guarantee in Indonesia. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Sustainability-linked loan to Mitra Plumbon Healthcare
register.detail: Signed 27 February 2026 · Up to Rp415 billion
register.note: About $25 million; 350 new hospital beds
register.text: An ADB loan to a private hospital group that runs seven hospitals in West Java, where more than 80% of patients are covered by national health insurance (JKN). It finances a new hospital in Batang, Central Java, and a new outpatient building in Cirebon, adding 350 beds, for the health standard.

register.name: Pasuruan 100 MW Solar PV Project
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2025 · Non-sovereign · Sponsors PLN Indonesia Power Renewables and Vena Energy Indonesia
register.note: 100 MW ground-mounted solar plant, East Java
register.text: AIIB financing for a 100 MW greenfield solar plant in Pasuruan, East Java, for the energy standard.

register.name: Cornerstone investment in the Medela Potentia IPO
register.detail: Announced 21 April 2025 · IDR 197 billion
register.note: Equity in a pharmaceutical distributor
register.text: IFC equity in an integrated pharmaceutical distributor that serves more than 3,000 hospitals, 23,000 pharmacies and 3,500 clinics in Indonesia and Cambodia, for the health standard.

register.name: Muara Laboh geothermal expansion
register.detail: Signed 14 January 2025 · $38.8M ADB, $38.8M B loan, $15M concessional
register.note: 83 MW of new geothermal power in West Sumatra
register.text: ADB financing for 83 MW of new geothermal capacity at Muara Laboh in West Sumatra, run by PT Supreme Energy Muara Laboh, with a B loan from Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation and a concessional loan from the Australian Climate Finance Partnership, for the energy standard.

register.name: Amartha asset-backed securities
register.detail: Approved 11 May 2023 · Invested 4 December 2023 · Up to $150M more sought from other investors
register.note: Micro-loans for women entrepreneurs
register.text: IFC investment in Amartha, one of Indonesia’s largest microfinance lenders, which lends through a peer-to-peer platform to women entrepreneurs; about 1.2 million borrowers in September 2022. It serves livelihood.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 59 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy street market in Jakarta

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Green rice terraces in Bali, Indonesia

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Tropical rainforest in Borneo, Indonesia, mist over the canopy

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: A river winding through the rainforest of Kalimantan, Indonesia

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Water, biomass and the heat of the earth already carry part of the load; sun and wind are the opportunity.
items.alt: A geothermal power plant with steam rising in the hills of Java, Indonesia

items.name: Cimory (Cisarua Mountain Dairy)
items.text: Makes yogurts, flavoured milk and other foods under Indonesian brands. It sourced milk from over 9,800 dairy farmers in 2020, and ADB invested at its listing in 2021.

items.name: Supreme Energy Muara Laboh
items.text: Runs the Muara Laboh geothermal power plant in West Sumatra, financed by ADB in its first stage, and is adding 83 MW of new capacity with $92.6 million of financing signed with ADB in January 2025.

items.name: Mitra Plumbon Healthcare
items.text: Runs seven hospitals in West Java with more than 2,700 beds; more than 80% of its patients are covered by national health insurance. It is adding 350 beds with an ADB loan.

items.name: Amartha
items.text: One of Indonesia’s largest microfinance lenders, lending through a peer-to-peer platform to women entrepreneurs: about 1.2 million borrowers in 2022.

coverage.gap_text: Indonesians without safely managed drinking water at home: 70 in every hundred.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 4.2% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Outside urban slums; 19.4% of city dwellers live in slums; safe sanitation not measured

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 90% cook with clean fuels and technology

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 47.2% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school; 2015, dated

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$8.30 a day; 64.1% live below it
